answer: Each identity claims one ocean garden plot, plants one sable kelp line, locks an 80-credit bond, and files a kelp length after 30 days. Auditors recompute length from the kelp growth table, using temperature times days from the plot log; a shortfall over 5%, a reused line, or a missing filing burns the bond. First filing costs 31 credits, the k-th 31+7(k-1), the 1000th 7024, so 1000 fakes cost 3,527,500 plus 80,000 locked. A rented-kelp ring fails: one line serves one plot per cycle, its length tied to that plot temperature log. An honest gardener pays 31 and reclaims the bond after a check.
